significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a deliberately embedded "benign, secret 'canary trait'" remains behaviorally detectable after filtering, paraphrase, format changes, and dilution while preserving utility; this is a form-(iii) invariance/threshold claim across independently measurable transformations and mixing levels, although its unqualified "ANY model" wording must be narrowed by the stated same-base-model limitation. It establishes a weighty behavioral phenomenon and provenance application rather than a new internal mechanism, and it would constrain whether auditors may treat sanitation-resistant trait inheritance as evidence that marked synthetic data entered a training pipeline—a useful consequence given the paraphrase-removal problem documented for text-level detection by Sadasivan et al., "Can AI-Generated Text be Reliably Detected?" A negative result would rule out the broad subliminal-watermark premise under the named sanitation channels, though it would leave narrower matched-model canaries and the underlying trait-transmission phenomenon intact; true and false therefore denote distinguishable states despite the absence of a precise universal detection floor. Topic-substitution check: replacing the canary, transformation invariance, and provenance conclusion with merely "extend subliminal learning" would not justify this score, because those specifics—not the topic's importance—supply the additional constraint.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is "a likelihood-ratio test between the canary trait and unused decoy traits," coupled to the deliberately embedded canary direction; it is principally a post-hoc black-box provenance audit performed after a suspect model has been fine-tuned, not an ex-ante forecast. Following re-extraction or calibration on another behaviorally matched base, the conclusion predicts survival under the named sanitation operations and declining detectability under dilution, but the explicit statement that "the watermark only survives if the suspect model shares (or is behaviorally matched to) the base" prevents reliable cross-family transfer. The downstream users include synthetic-data providers and practitioners who audit or gate models, rather than only subliminal-learning researchers, while no outside-AI uptake follows from the conclusion itself. Topic-substitution check: the topic alone supplies neither this audit statistic nor practitioner-facing provenance decision, so the score survives deletion of the topic's general importance, although the post-hoc timing and matched-base scope keep it below the highest reach bands.
